# Epsylo

> Epsylo is a translation app that explains itself. Every translation comes with a word-by-word breakdown: each segment is colour-coded by grammatical role and shown with its dictionary form, an explanation and alternatives, plus syntax cards and dependency trees. It is built for language learners who want to understand why a sentence is put together the way it is, not only what it means.

Epsylo works on the learner's own sentences. Instead of fixed drills or a set course, you type or paste something you want to say or read, and Epsylo translates it and breaks down the grammar of that exact sentence.

## Who it is for

- Language learners at any level who want grammar explained on real sentences they care about.
- Learners who already use flashcards or a course and want a tool for "why is it said this way?" questions.
- People reading or writing in a foreign language who want to check word order, particles, cases, conjugations and politeness.

## Core features

- Word-by-word breakdown: each segment colour-coded by grammatical role, with dictionary form, explanation and alternatives.
- Syntax cards and dependency trees showing how the words in a sentence relate.
- Live controls: politeness from blunt to honorific (four levels) and emphasis, which can target single words. The translation and its breakdown update as you change them.
- Vocabulary bank with spaced review, stored on your device, works offline.
- 97 languages. English, Italian, Japanese and Spanish have hand-written language profiles; the other 93 are marked Beta.

## How it differs from drill-based grammar apps

- Drill apps teach grammar through pre-written exercises. Epsylo explains the grammar of whatever sentence you give it.
- The explanation is attached to a translation, so you see meaning and structure together.
- Politeness and emphasis are adjustable, so you can see how a sentence changes in register.

## Pricing

- Free plan: 20 translations a month.
